- **Well, that didn’t last long 😊! After what feels like the first proper summer reset in 30 years and with our Croatian road trip on the horizon it feels like the right moment to share what’s next. From late October, I’ll be joining forces with Kanga Health Ltd as a Senior Strategist. It’s a move I’m genuinely excited about, not just because of the work, but because of the people: I’ve known the Kanga team for years and have always found them smart, thoughtful, creative, and very grounded in what actually matters to clients (speaking from experience😊). I’ll be focusing on the areas I’ve always most enjoyed; customer engagement, CX, AI transformation, omnichannel strategy, capability building and commercial/launch excellence, helping teams cut through the friction and focus on the things that create real impact. And, as an early opportunity to get out and meet people in the new role, I’ll be joining the Kanga crew in Vienna for NEXT CX & AI 26 (27th-28th October). If you’re there to come and say hello, there should be plenty to talk about. For anyone in pharma, health, and life sciences who wants to connect, collaborate, or just swap notes or indeed discuss the best of Croatia I’d be delighted to hear from you. - **And so… one week ago today I closed a chapter that’s shaped almost every part of my life. After 30 years with Pfizer, I left an amazing company. I seen that moment coming for months, but it still knocked me sideways! When I finished up last Tuesday, I found myself thinking about the three decades of memories: the early mornings, the late nights, the wins, the tough days, the product launches, the travel… but most of all, the people. These people weren’t just across the UK, they were everywhere, from Australia to Japan to Brazil to the US and pretty much everywhere in between! I’ve been lucky enough to work with amazing colleagues from all over the world, each bringing their own energy, humour, culture and way of thinking. I’m not going to pretend I can wrap 30 years into one message, but I can say this: I’ve spent my career surrounded by genuinely brilliant people who show up every day to do amazing work that matters. People who care. People who push. People who have made me better. I couldn’t be prouder to have stood alongside you! I’ve tried to figure out how to say thank you to the hundreds of colleagues, mentors and friends the ones who challenged me, supported me, laughed with me, and occasionally told me the hard truths I needed to hear but the reality is you can’t without missing someone, but you know who you are! There’s no perfect way to say it, so I’ll keep it simple: thank you, truly and deeply, thank you! There is one exception however, I can top and tail 30 years! So, to the three people who took a chance on a rookie 30 years ago John Young , Joan Campbell and Easton McCracken (RIP), quite simply you changed the direction of my life. I walked in unsure of myself and you saw something I hadn't yet seen. I’ve carried that with me every day since. Words will never be enough, but they’re what I have: thank you from the bottom of my heart! And as I closed this chapter, I want to thank the 2 people who helped me finish strong. Jorge Herrera, CCXP and Daniel Blatt you’ve been the kind of colleagues everyone hopes to find. You made the last stretch not just meaningful, but genuinely joyful. You guys rock! To my team João Lóios Dawar Ali Khan Sarah Holiday Sal Shukla Madhu Mishra Mary Geraty Jennifer W. Franny Eklund Jessica Chau thank you! Thirty years, it’s been a privilege. And now… some down time, a road trip in September, and whatever comes next ( Audrey Catriona Gent 😊). I can’t wait! ...more**

When we combine the right technology, data and content with genuine customer understanding, personalization becomes something much more powerful: a way to put the customer first and consistently surpass expectations. - **Today marks my first day of a week off with nothing in the diary for the first time in memory. No holiday, no wedding, no house project etcetera. Modern life fills every gap because empty time makes us uneasy, and most of us rarely leave any. This week I have no agenda, just space to think and be around the people who matter, something we don't get the chance to do often enough. Plan for day one- try to enjoy keeping pace with a two year old who's already faster than me. Getting better at doing nothing!**
